docs.title: Management of medication
docs.subtitle: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Quality Indicators for NDIS Practice Standards) Guidelines 2018, section 26. Compilation 3, in force 1 July 2026. Rules Schedule 1, clause 26.
docs.html:
1Outcome

Each participant requiring medication is confident their provider administers, stores and monitors the effects of their medication and works to prevent errors or incidents.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Records clearly identify the medication and dosage required by each participant, including all information required to correctly identify the participant and to safely administer the medication.

(2)

All workers responsible for administering medication understand the effects and side-effects of the medication and the steps to take in the event of an incident involving medication.

(3)

All medications are stored safely and securely, can be easily identified and differentiated, and are only accessed by appropriately trained workers.

questions.text: What are the date and time of the call?
questions.hint: Write the time the call started.

questions.text: Who gave the order? Give their full name, profession and practice.
questions.hint: Only the participant's prescriber gives an order. Write their registration number if they give it. If you do not know them, check the national public register of health practitioners.

questions.text: Which number did you call back on, and where did it come from?
questions.hint: Call back on the practice number in the participant's file (the prescriber's practice number on the chart) or the practice's own published number. Never use a number the caller gives you. If you cannot call back, stop.

questions.text: Who took the order? Give your full name, role, registration number and what lets you take it.
questions.hint: Say which: registered nurse, or the authority the medicines law of [state or territory] gives you, and name the provision of that law recorded under POL-HID-08 Ground rule 4. A worker who is not an order taker never takes an order.

questions.text: Was a second listener present?
questions.hint: A second listener is another registered nurse or, failing that, a trained worker. They witness the read-back; they do not take the order. Name them and their role. Never delay an urgent order to find one. Write "no witness" if there is none.

questions.text: What are the participant's full name and date of birth?
questions.hint: Copy them from the chart (the participant's name and date of birth on the chart). Ask the prescriber to say them. A different name or date means a different person: stop.

questions.text: What is the participant's number or address?
questions.hint: This is the third identifier on the chart.

questions.text: Which allergies and bad reactions did you read to the prescriber, and what did the prescriber say?
questions.hint: Copy them from the chart's allergy and adverse reaction entry and read every one aloud. Write "nil known" only if the chart says so.

questions.text: Which plan, and which earlier order or chart line, does this order change?
questions.hint: Give the date of the plan (FRM-HID-01) and the date of the order. Write "new medicine" if there is none.

questions.text: What is the medicine? Give its generic name, strength and form.
questions.hint: Use the generic name. Spell it back to the prescriber. "Same as before" is not an answer.

questions.text: What is the dose, and what is the route?
questions.hint: Write the dose as a number with the word "units", in full. Never write "U" or "IU". The route must be subcutaneous. If it is not, stop.

questions.text: How often, and at what times?
questions.hint: Use the 24 hour clock. "Daily" alone is not enough.

questions.text: What is the medicine for?
questions.hint: Use plain words the participant would use.

questions.text: When does it start, and when does it stop or get reviewed?
questions.hint: Give the start date, and the stop date, the number of doses or the date the prescriber will review it. For a hold-one-dose order, write the dose held and the next dose due. Any other order with no end or review date is not accepted.

questions.text: If the medicine is only for when it is needed: what is the reason, the shortest time between doses and the most in 24 hours?
questions.hint: Copy all three from the prescriber. An as-needed order missing any of them cannot be used.
questions.optional: Yes, when the medicine is not as needed

questions.text: What kind of change is this?
questions.hint: Check PRO-HID-07 Decision table 1. If the table says "do not take it", stop and ask for a written order.

options: change a fixed dose or time
other: do not take it, ask for a written order

questions.section: Section D: The injection (order taker for questions 17 and 18; Service Manager for questions 19 and 20)
questions.text: What device, and which injection sites?
questions.hint: Pen, pre-filled syringe, or vial and syringe. Name a site only if the prescriber changes it. Otherwise write "as the plan". Needle length and angle belong to the plan: do not change them here.

questions.section: Section D: The injection (order taker for questions 17 and 18; Service Manager for questions 19 and 20)
questions.text: Is a reading needed before the dose?
questions.hint: Write "no reading needed" if none. A phone order cannot change the plan's limits (PRO-HID-07 Decision table 1). If the prescriber wants to change a hold or call limit, do not take that part: ask for a written order and a plan update. FRM-HID-12 Section A is then re-done and checked before the next reading.

questions.section: Section D: The injection (order taker for questions 17 and 18; Service Manager for questions 19 and 20)
questions.text: Which trained workers may give it?
questions.hint: The Service Manager completes this after the call. Name each worker. Check each name in REG-HID-01. A worker who is not signed off for this medicine and device cannot give it.

questions.section: Section D: The injection (order taker for questions 17 and 18; Service Manager for questions 19 and 20)
questions.text: Does any worker need briefing or training before the first dose?
questions.hint: The Service Manager completes this after the call. Say who will do it and by when. A changed device or dose needs the worker signed off for it first.

questions.section: Section E: Read-back and what to watch for (order taker)
questions.text: Did you read the whole order back to the prescriber, and did they confirm it?
questions.hint: Read every item aloud: participant, medicine, dose in units, route, times and dates. Wait for the prescriber to say it is correct. If they correct anything, read it all again.

questions.section: Section E: Read-back and what to watch for (order taker)
questions.text: What did the prescriber say to watch for, and when to call back?
questions.hint: Take this from the prescriber. Add when to call 000.

questions.section: Section E: Read-back and what to watch for (order taker)
questions.text: Who do workers phone with questions about this order, and at which numbers?
questions.hint: Give the practice number, and an after-hours number if there is one.

questions.section: Section F: The prescriber's written confirmation
questions.text: By when is the written confirmation due, and how will the prescriber send it?
questions.hint: Due time is the time the medicines law of [state or territory] sets, and in any case no later than 24 hours after the call. Name how: secure message, fax, email or e-prescription.

questions.section: Section F: The prescriber's written confirmation
questions.text: When did it arrive, and who checked it against this record?
questions.hint: The Service Manager completes this. Compare the medicine, strength, dose, route, times and dates. Write "not arrived" until it does.

questions.section: Section F: The prescriber's written confirmation
questions.text: Did it match this record? If not, what differs and what was done?
questions.hint: If it differs, phone the prescriber the same day. Give no more doses from the phone order until the prescriber says which is right.

questions.section: Section F: The prescriber's written confirmation
questions.text: If it did not arrive by the due time, what was done?
questions.hint: The order has lapsed. Say who was told, who gave advice about the next dose, and what that advice was.
questions.optional: Yes, only when it arrived on time

questions.section: Section G: The chart, the participant and the plan (Service Manager)
questions.text: Who put the order on the chart, who checked the line, and when?
questions.hint: Name the Service Manager and the chart checker. The chart line names this record as its source and is marked "phone order, confirmation due".

questions.section: Section G: The chart, the participant and the plan (Service Manager)
questions.text: Was the participant, or their decision maker, told about the change, and what did they say?
questions.hint: Tell them in their usual way of communicating, before the next dose. Say who told them, when, and what they said. A signature is never a condition of urgent treatment. If they do not agree, phone the prescriber. No worker overrides them.

questions.section: Section G: The chart, the participant and the plan (Service Manager)
questions.text: Does this order change the participant's plan?
questions.hint: If yes, say what changes, who told the health practitioner and when the plan will be updated. A changed plan means each worker is assessed again before the next injection.

form.intro:
This record holds one medication order that a prescriber gives by phone or by word of mouth, for a participant who has subcutaneous injections. Only an order taker completes it, and only where POL-HID-08 Subcutaneous Injections Policy Ground rule 4 records that the medicines law of [state or territory] allows a phone order. A worker who is not an order taker never takes an order and never acts on one. PRO-HID-07 Subcutaneous Injections Procedure, step 9, says what a worker does when a prescriber calls.

Who completes it, and when:

  • Sections A to E: the order taker, during the call. Take questions 6, 10, 11, 12, 14, 21 and 22 first, while the prescriber is on the line; complete the rest from the chart straight after the call. Questions 19 and 20 are the Service Manager's.
  • Section F: the order taker sets the due time during the call. The Service Manager completes the rest when the written confirmation arrives.
  • Section G, and questions 19 and 20: the Service Manager, before the next dose of the medicine is due.

Have ready: the participant's chart (FRM-MED-01) and plan (FRM-HID-01), the practice's phone number from the participant's file, and a pen. If a second listener is near, ask them to listen.

Storage, self-management and general consent belong in the participant's medication plan (FRM-MED-02) and the participant's support plan, not here.

What happens next: the Service Manager puts the order on the chart, tells the participant and briefs the trained workers. The Service Manager then checks the prescriber's written confirmation. The record is filed with the chart.

Every copy of this record carries these lines:

  • A worker who is not an order taker and is phoned an order takes a message only. The worker does not write down or act on the order.
  • A phone order cannot start a medicine, change a dose scale or a reading limit, or change insulin or a blood thinner. PRO-HID-07 Decision table 1 lists what a phone order can and cannot do.
  • The prescriber's written confirmation is due within the time the medicines law of [state or territory] sets, and in any case within 24 hours of the call. If it is late, the order has lapsed and no worker gives a dose from it.
  • If you cannot read the order back to the prescriber, do not accept it.
  • This record is used only where the Quality Manager has recorded, under POL-HID-08 Ground rule 4, the provision of the medicines law of [state or territory] that allows the order taker to take a phone order: [provision, recorded at adoption]. Where no provision is recorded, every order comes in writing.
form.privacy:
This record holds health information about the participant. We collect it so that a phone order is written down in full, read back, confirmed in writing and acted on safely. It also shows who said what and when.

The order taker, the Service Manager, the trained workers named at question 19, the Clinical Lead and the Quality Manager read it. With the participant's consent we share it with their prescriber, their pharmacist and other health services. In an emergency we give it to ambulance or hospital staff where the law allows. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form records the consent.

If you are the participant, you can ask to see this record and ask us to correct it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.

The record also holds the names, roles and phone numbers of the prescriber and the order taker. We keep them so the order can be traced to the people who gave and took it.
form.after:
• Order taker: give the completed record to the Service Manager, or to the on-call manager after hours, straight after the read-back. Say which dose is due next (our standard).
  • Service Manager: put the order on the chart, tell the participant and brief the trained workers. Do this before the next dose of that medicine is due (our standard). PRO-HID-07 step 4 sets how.
  • Service Manager: check the written confirmation as soon as it arrives, and again at the due time (our standard). PRO-HID-07 step 11 sets how.
  • Service Manager: file the record with the chart in the participant's file within 7 days of the confirmation check (our standard).
  • Quality Manager: sample these records in the 3 month desk review and the 6 month injection audit under PRO-HID-07 step 30.
  • Keep each record for 7 years after its last entry (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026: records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years). The health records law of [state or territory] can require longer, and so can a record about a child.

signs.confirms: "I heard the order and the read-back."
